a:r.a:t: I trained and evaluated two forecasting approaches: XGBoost and SARIMA.

XGBoost is the default model in the app. It uses the lag and calendar features from the previous slide, and it forecasts recursively. That means for a multi-week forecast, the model predicts the next week, feeds that prediction back into the lag features, and continues forward for the selected horizon.

SARIMA is my baseline time-series model. It is a univariate seasonal model using the specification SARIMA(1,1,1)(1,1,1,52). The seasonal period of 52 is chosen because the data is weekly and gasoline prices often show annual seasonality.

For evaluation, I used a 52-week holdout window. XGBoost performed better on this holdout. Its MAE is about 0.0579 dollars per gallon and RMSE is about 0.1004. SARIMA's MAE is about 0.2386 and RMSE is about 0.4217.

The main interpretation is that recent lagged prices carry a strong short-term signal. SARIMA gives a useful time-series baseline, but in this project the lag-based XGBoost model captured the short-term structure better. That is why XGBoost is the default option in the deployed app, while SARIMA remains available for comparison.
